headline: One-time UK tax benefit swings MPT back to a profit
summary_short: MPT's Q1 2026 revenue rose 12.6% y/y to $252.1M on retenanted Steward properties, while net income swung to $32.8M ($0.05 diluted EPS) from a $118.3M loss a year ago on lower impairments and a one-time UK tax benefit.
summary_long: Net income of $32.8M ($0.05/share) reversed a $118.3M prior-year loss, driven by $28.3M higher revenue (mostly re-tenanted Steward rents), a $43M one-time U.K. REIT tax benefit, and lower impairments ($19.0M vs $76.1M). Interest expense rose to $133.3M as average borrowings and rates (5.2% vs 4.9%) increased. Operating cash flow was -$14.3M on higher interest paid; management expects improvement as HSA/NOR rents ramp up. Cash fell to $425.0M q/q, funding dividends, Prospect bankruptcy commitments, and debt paydown; long-term debt and equity both edged lower q/q. Normalized FFO held flat at $0.14/diluted share. No formal guidance was reiterated in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Net income improved because higher retenanted rents and a $43M one-time U.K. REIT deferred-tax benefit outweighed higher interest expense; the swing from a prior-year loss also reflects far smaller impairment charges ($19.0M vs $76.1M a year ago).

Revenue rose $28.3M (12.6%) y/y, primarily $15.5M more rent from re-tenanting former Steward facilities, $2.5M from 2025-2026 acquisitions, $7.5M of favorable FX, and CPI-linked escalators, partly offset by lower property-sale revenue.

Net income swung to a profit mainly on the revenue increase, a $43M one-time deferred-tax benefit from moving seven U.K. entities into the U.K. REIT, and materially lower impairment and fair-value charges than the prior-year quarter.
EPS moved in step with net income; weighted-average diluted shares were slightly lower y/y (597.7M vs 600.6M), adding a small incremental lift to per-share EPS.
Not broken out as a standalone line in the release; the y/y increase is consistent with higher revenue and materially lower impairment charges flowing through operating results.
Not explained as a standalone EBITDA line; the outsized y/y increase reflects the prior-year quarter's $76.1M of impairment charges and $45.2M of other expense, both far smaller in the 2026 quarter.

The filing does not use 'cost of revenue' terminology; the rise is consistent with $5.1M higher real estate depreciation ($69.7M vs $64.6M) and $2.9M higher non-reimbursed property expenses ($9.9M vs $7.0M) disclosed separately in the MD&A.

Pretax income rose from a $108.6M loss to near breakeven mainly on the revenue increase and $57M less impairment/fair-value charges, before the separate $32.8M tax benefit that further lifted net income.

Operating cash flow fell to -$14.3M, driven by a $56M y/y increase in interest paid tied to 2025 refinancing activity, partly offset by $33M more cash rent received and lower litigation/bankruptcy cash costs.

Cash fell q/q as proceeds from asset sales and the revolving Credit Facility funded dividends, the $45M Prospect bankruptcy funding commitment, and other investing activity; not broken out as a single reconciling driver in the release.
Not explained as a standalone line; the modest q/q decline is consistent with net paydown of the revolving portion of the Credit Facility during the quarter.
Not explained as a standalone line; the q/q decline is consistent with $0.09/share of dividends declared exceeding net income, plus an other-comprehensive-loss currency translation hit.
